questions.question: If 4 men or 6 boys can finish a piece of work in 20 days, then in how many days can 6 men and 11 boys finish the same work?
questions.questionHtml: If 4 men or 6 boys can finish a piece of work in 20 days, then in how many days can 6 men and 11 boys finish the same work?
questions.solution:
4 men = 6 boys 

⇒ Then, 1 boy = 4/6 men = 2/3 men 

⇒ 11 boys = 2/3 × 11 men = 22/3 men 

⇒ Then, 6 men + 11 boys = 6 + (22/3) = 40/3 men 

⇒ 1 work done = 4 men × 20 days 

⇒ 4 × 20 = 40/3 × d days ⇒  d = 2 x 3 = 6

questions.question: Mitu can do a piece of work in 12 hours, Titu and Situ together in 2 hours, and Mitu and Situ together in 3 hours. How long will Titu alone take to do it?
questions.questionHtml: Mitu can do a piece of work in 12 hours, Titu and Situ together in 2 hours, and Mitu and Situ together in 3 hours. How long will Titu alone take to do it?
questions.solution:
Mitu's work per hour = 1/12

Titu and Situ's combined work per hour = 1/2

Mitu and Situ's combined work per hour = 1/3

Situ's work per hour: 1/S = 1/3 - 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4, S = 4 hours

Titu's work per hour: 1/T + 1/4 = 1/2, 1/T = 1/2 - 1/4 = 1/4, T = 4 hours

questions.question: George can do 35% of the total work in 6 days. Jim and George together completed a piece of work in 12 days. In how many days could Jim, working alone, complete the entire task?
questions.questionHtml: George can do 35% of the total work in 6 days. Jim and George together completed a piece of work in 12 days. In how many days could Jim, working alone, complete the entire task?
questions.solution:
Efficiency Person Time Total work
7 George 120/7 120
10 Jim + George 12

Efficiency of Jim + George = 10 units/day ⇒ Jim + 7 = 10 ⇒ Efficiency of Jim = 10 - 7 = 3. Total time taken to do the entire work = 120/3 = 40 days

questions.question: Vaibhav can do a piece of work in 60 days. He works there for 15 days and then Sandeep alone finishes the remaining work in 30 days. In how many days will Vaibhav and Sandeep working together finish the work?
questions.questionHtml: Vaibhav can do a piece of work in 60 days. He works there for 15 days and then Sandeep alone finishes the remaining work in 30 days. In how many days will Vaibhav and Sandeep working together finish the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

Vaibhav can do a piece of work = 60 days

Number of days Vaibhav works = 15 days

Sandeep alone finish the remaining work = 30 days

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

Total work = 60

Let efficiency of Sandeep be x, then

15 + 30x = 60

30x = 60 – 15 = 45

x = 45/30 = 1.5

Vaibhav and Sandeep together can complete the whole work in = 60/(1 + 1.5) = 60/2.5 = 24 days

Alternate Method

Suppose Sandeep can complete the whole work in x days. 

According to the question,

15/60 + 30/x = 1

⇒ 30/x = 1 – 1/4

⇒ 30/x = 3/4

⇒ x = 40 days

Vaibhav and Sandeep together can complete the work in 1 day = 1/60 + 1/40

⇒ (2 + 3)/120 = 5/120 = 1/24

∴ Vaibhav and Sandeep together can complete the whole work in 24 days.

Alternate MethodCalculation:

Time taken by Vaibhav to complete the work = (60/15) = 4 days

Number of days Sandeep works = (1 – 1/4) = 3/4 days

Time taken by Sandeep to complete the work = (4/3 × 30) = 40 days

Now,

LCM of 60 and 40 is 120

Efficiency of Vaibhav = (120/60) = 2 units/day

Efficiency of Sandeep = (120/40) = 3 units/day

Time taken by Vaibhav and Sandeep together to complete a work = [120/(2 + 3)]

⇒ 120/5 days

⇒ 24 days

∴ The required days is 24 days.

questions.question: 12 men can do a work in 8 days while 4 boys can do it in 40 days. In how many days 9 boys and 3 men together will complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: 12 men can do a work in 8 days while 4 boys can do it in 40 days. In how many days 9 boys and 3 men together will complete the same work?
questions.solution:
12M × 8 = 4B × 40 ⇒ 3M = 5B ⇒ M : B = 5 : 3

Total work = 12 × 5 × 8 = 480

9 boys and 3 men together will complete the same work in = 480/(9 × 3 + 3 × 5)

⇒ 480/42 ⇒ 80/7 days

questions.question: Four men and 6 women can complete a certain piece of work in 5 days whereas three men and 4 women can complete it in 7 days. How many men should assist 25 women to complete \(2\frac{1}{2}\) times the same work in 5 days?
questions.questionHtml: Four men and 6 women can complete a certain piece of work in 5 days whereas three men and 4 women can complete it in 7 days. How many men should assist 25 women to complete \(2\frac{1}{2}\) times the same work in 5 days?
questions.solution:
Let efficiency of 1 man and 1 woman be x and y respectively.

Total work = (4x + 6y) × 5     ------ (1)

Total work = (3x + 4y) × 7     ------ (2)

From equation (1) and equation (2)

(4x + 6y) × 5 = (3x + 4y) × 7

⇒ 20x + 30y = 21x + 28y

⇒ 21x – 20x = 30y – 28y

⇒ x = 2y

⇒ x : y = 2 : 1

Efficiency of 1 man = 2

Efficiency of 1 woman = 1

Total work = (4x + 6y) × 5 = (4 × 2 + 6 × 1) × 5 = 70

2 times of total work = 70 × 5/2 = 175

Let the number of men be n, then

According to the question

(2n + 1 × 25) 5 = 175

⇒ 2n + 25 = 175/5 = 35

⇒ 2n = 35 – 25 = 10

⇒ n = 10/2 = 5

So, the number of men are 5.

questions.question: 3 men, 4 women and 6 children can complete a work in 7 days. A woman does double the work a man does and a child does half the work a man does. How many women alone can complete this work in 7 days?
questions.questionHtml: 3 men, 4 women and 6 children can complete a work in 7 days. A woman does double the work a man does and a child does half the work a man does. How many women alone can complete this work in 7 days?
questions.solution:
Given∶

Time taken by 3 men, 4 women, 6 children to complete the work = 7 days.

A woman does double work compare to a man and a child does half work compare to a man.

Ratio of efficiency of man and woman = 1 ∶ 2,

Ratio of efficiency of child and man = 1 ∶ 2

Calculation∶

Ratio of efficiency of man, woman and child = 2 ∶ 4 ∶ 1

Total work = (3 man + 4 woman + 6 child) × 7 days = (3 × 2 + 4 × 4 + 6 × 1) × 7 = 28 × 7 = 196

Number of women necessary to complete to the work in 7 days = 196/(4 × 7) = 7

questions.question: P and Q completed a work together and were paid ₹ 1,080 and ₹ 1,440, respectively. If P can do the entire work in 20 days, how many days did they take to complete the work together?
questions.questionHtml: P and Q completed a work together and were paid ₹1,080 and ₹1,440, respectively. If P can do the entire work in 20 days, how many days did they take to complete the work together?
questions.solution:
Ratio of amount paid to P and Q = 1080 : 1440 ⇒ 3 : 4

Now, Total work = 20 × 3 ⇒ 60 units

So, time taken by both of them to complete the work = 60/7 ⇒ \(8{4\over7}\) days

questions.question: Work can be completed by 8 boys in 48 days. If 2 boys leave after working for 24 days, then how many days will be needed to complete the remaining work?
questions.questionHtml: Work can be completed by 8 boys in 48 days. If 2 boys leave after working for 24 days, then how many days will be needed to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
(8 × 48) = (8 × 24) + 6d = 192 = 6 × d = d = 192/6

Time is taken to complete remaining work = 32 days

questions.question: A is 3 times as fast as B and is, therefore, able to complete a work in 32 days lesser than B. A and B, working together, can complete the work in ______.
questions.questionHtml: A is 3 times as fast as B and is, therefore, able to complete a work in 32 days lesser than B. A and B, working together, can complete the work in ______.
questions.solution:
Work efficiency of A and B = 3 : 1

Time ratio will be 1 : 3 and Ratio difference = 3 – 1 = 2

Time Difference = 32 days

⇒ Ratio of 2 = 32 days, Ratio of 1 = 16 days

A alone completes the work in 16 days and B completes in 16 × 3 = 48 days.

LCM of 16 and 48 = 48

Time in which both can complete the work together = \(\frac{48}{3+1}=\frac{48}{4}=12\) days

questions.question: A, B and C can all together do a piece of work in 10 days, in which B takes 3 times as long as A and C together to do the work. In how many days can B alone do the work?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C can all together do a piece of work in 10 days, in which B takes 3 times as long as A and C together to do the work. In how many days can B alone do the work?
questions.solution:
B takes 3 times as long as A and C together to do the work, so the efficiency of (A + C) : B = 3 : 1   [ as efficiency ∝ 1/time ]

A, B and C can all together do a piece of work in 10 days, so total work = (3 + 1) × 10 = 40 unit

Now, B alone can do this in 40/1 = 40 days

questions.question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 30 days, 45 days and 90 days, respectively. A starts the work and he is assisted by B and C together every third day. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 30 days, 45 days and 90 days, respectively. A starts the work and he is assisted by B and C together every third day. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
Total work = 90

Work done by A, B and C in 3 days = 3A + B + C = 3 × 3 + 2 + 1 = 12

Work done by A, B and C in 21 days = 12 × 7 = 84

Remaining work = 90 – 84 = 6

A will complete 6 unit work in 6/3 = 2 days

Total days = 21 + 2 = 23

questions.question: A works 3.5 times as fast as B, and A takes 45 days less than B to complete a job when each works alone. Calculate the number of days taken to complete the same job if A and B work together.
questions.questionHtml: A works 3.5 times as fast as B, and A takes 45 days less than B to complete a job when each works alone. Calculate the number of days taken to complete the same job if A and B work together.
questions.solution:
Let us assume the time taken by A and B is 2x and 7x.

The difference in the number of days A and B = 45

⇒ 7x - 2x = 45 ⇒ x = 45/5 = 9

So, Total Work = 9 × 14 = 126 units

Work completed by A and B in days = 126/9 = 14 days

questions.question: If 2 men or 4 women can build a wall in 34 days, in how many days can 6 men and 5 women build the same wall?
questions.questionHtml: If 2 men or 4 women can build a wall in 34 days, in how many days can 6 men and 5 women build the same wall?
questions.solution:
Let the efficiency of one man and woman be a and b respectively.

Then using concept,  2a × 34 = 4b × 34 ⇒ a = 2b

Now, total work = 4b × 34 = 136b 

Efficiency of 6 men and 5 women = 6a + 5b = 17b

Hence, time taken = total work / efficiency

⇒ 136b / 17b ⇒ 8

questions.question: To complete a certain task, X is 40% more efficient than Y, and Z is 40% less efficient than Y. Working together, they can complete the task in 21 days. Y and Z together worked for 35 days. The remaining work will be completed by X alone in:
questions.questionHtml: To complete a certain task, X is 40% more efficient than Y, and Z is 40% less efficient than Y. Working together, they can complete the task in 21 days. Y and Z together worked for 35 days. The remaining work will be completed by X alone in:
questions.solution:
Let efficiency of y be 5 unit

Efficiency of X = 5 × (7/5) = 7

Efficiency of Z = 5 × (3/5) = 3

Total work = (5 + 7 + 3) × 21 = 315

Work done by y and Z in 35 days = (5 + 3) × 35 = 280

Remaining work = 315 – 280 = 35

∴Remaining work will be completed by X alone in = 35/7 = 5 days

questions.question: Sixteen men can finish a work in 8 days. Eight men and nine women working together can finish the same work in 10 days. In how many days will twenty women finish the same work?
questions.questionHtml: Sixteen men can finish a work in 8 days. Eight men and nine women working together can finish the same work in 10 days. In how many days will twenty women finish the same work?
questions.solution:
Let the efficiency of 1 man and 1 woman are x and y respectively

According to the question

16m × 8 = (8m + 9w) × 10

⇒ 128m = 80m + 90w

⇒ 128m – 80m = 90w

⇒ 48m = 90w

m : w = 15 : 8

Total work  = 16 × 15 × 8

Let 20 women complete the whole work in x days,

⇒ 20 × 8 × x = 16 × 15 × 8

⇒ x = 12 days

questions.question: A and B separately can build a wall in 12 and 16 days, respectively. If they work for 1 day alternatively, starting with A, in how many days will the wall be built?
questions.questionHtml: A and B separately can build a wall in 12 and 16 days, respectively. If they work for 1 day alternatively, starting with A, in how many days will the wall be built?
questions.solution:
Given :

A can do a work in 12 days 

B can do the same work in 16 days 

They work on alternate days 

Concept used :

work done each day = total work/total number of days

Calculations :

Total work = LCM of 12 and 16 

⇒ 48 units 

A's per day work = 48/12 = 4 units 

B's per day work = 48/16 = 3 units 

Total work done in 13 days  (7 days of A and 6 days of B) = 7 × 4 + 6 × 3 = 46 units 

Remaining work = 48 – 46 = 2 units 

Time is taken by B to complete the remaining work = 2/3  (B's turn to do the work)

⇒ 2/3 days

Total time taken = 13 + 2/3 

⇒ \(13{2\ \over3}\)  days

∴ Total \(13{2\ \over3}\) days will be taken to complete the work

questions.question: A can complete 3/8 part of a work in 36 days. B can complete 1/2 part of the same work in 27 days. Which of the following statement(s) is are correct? I. A is less efficient than B. II. A and B working together can complete 11/15 part of the same work in 36 days.
questions.questionHtml:
A can complete 3/8 part of a work in 36 days. B can complete 1/2 part of the same work in 27 days. Which of the following statement(s) is are correct? 

I. A is less efficient than B.

II. A and B working together can complete 11/15 part of the same work in 36 days.
questions.solution:
A's full work will take (36 / 3) × 8 = 96 days.

B's full work will take (27 / 1) × 2 = 54 days.

I. A is less efficient than B - Correct, since A takes more time than B.

II. A and B working together can complete 11/15 work in 36 days - Incorrect, as working together they can complete (1/96 + 1/54) × 36 = ~0.73 of the work in 36 days.

questions.question: Two men and 7 women can complete a work in 28 days whereas 6 men and 16 women can do the same work in 11 days. In how many days can 7 men complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: Two men and 7 women can complete a work in 28 days whereas 6 men and 16 women can do the same work in 11 days. In how many days can 7 men complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

2 men and 7 women can complete a work = 28 days

6 men and 16 women can complete a work = 11 days

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

According to the question

⇒ (2m + 7w) × 28 = (6m + 16w) × 11

⇒ 56m + 196w = 66m + 176w

⇒ 10m = 20w

⇒ m/w = 2/1

Total work = (2 × 2 + 7 × 1) × 28

⇒ (4 + 7) × 28

⇒ 11 × 28

⇒ 308

Time taken by 7 men to complete the work = (308/7 × 2)

⇒ (308/14)

⇒ 22 days

∴ Required days is 22.

questions.question: A and B alone can do a piece of work in 4 and 9 days, respectively. In how many days will the work be completed, if they both work on alternate days, starting with B?
questions.questionHtml: A and B alone can do a piece of work in 4 and 9 days, respectively. In how many days will the work be completed, if they both work on alternate days, starting with B?
questions.solution:
Efficiency Person Time Total work
9 A 4 36
4 B 9

(B + A) = 4 + 9 = 13 units = 2 days ⇒ 30 units = 5 days ⇒ 36 units = 5 + (6/9) = 5\(2\over3\) days

questions.question: 40 men can complete a work in 15 days. Five days after they started working, 10 more men joined them. In how many days will the total work be completed?
questions.questionHtml: 40 men can complete a work in 15 days. Five days after they started working, 10 more men joined them. In how many days will the total work be completed?
questions.solution:
40 men can complete the work in 15 days.

Total work = 40 × 15 = 600 man-days

Work done in 5 days by 40 men = 40 × 5 = 200 man-days

Remaining work = 600 - 200 = 400 man-days

50 men now (40 + 10) ⇒ Days to complete remaining work = 400 / 50 = 8 days

Total days = 5 + 8 = 13 days

questions.question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 11 days, 20 days and 55 days respectively. How soon can the work be done if A works with B on first day, A works with C on second day and so on?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 11 days, 20 days and 55 days respectively. How soon can the work be done if A works with B on first day, A works with C on second day and so on?
questions.solution:
​Total work = LCM ( 11 , 20 & 55 ) = 220

Efficiency of  A =  \(\frac{220}{11}\) = 20

⇒ Efficiency of  B =  11 ⇒ Efficiency of  C = 4

A works with B on the first day = 20 + 11 = 31

A works with C on the second day = 20 + 4 = 24

In two days total work = 31+ 24 = 55

Total pairs days of  required work 

⇒  \(\frac{220}{55}\)  =  4

So,4 ×  2 = 8 days of completed work.

questions.question: A and B together can complete a certain work in 20 days whereas B and C together can complete it in 24 days. If A is twice as good a workman as C, then in what time will B alone do 40% of the same work?
questions.questionHtml: A and B together can complete a certain work in 20 days whereas B and C together can complete it in 24 days. If A is twice as good a workman as C, then in what time will B alone do 40% of the same work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A = 2C

A + B in 20 days

B + C in 24 days

Concept used:

Total work = LCM of time taken by the workers

Calculation:

LCM of 20 and 24 is 120

So, efficiency of A and B = 120/20 = 6 and efficiency of B and C = 120/24 = 5

Now 2C + B = 6 and B + C = 5

So, C = 1

B = 4

40% of the work = 120 × 2/5 = 48 units

So, B will take 48/4 = 12 days

∴ B alone do 40% of the same work in 12 days

Shortcut Trick

Now 2C + B = 6 and B + C = 5

So, C = 1

B = 4

So,

A, B and C = 2, 4, and 1

40% of the work = 120 × 2/5 = 48 units

So, B will take 48/4 = 12 days

questions.question: A and B can finish a job in 10 days and 5 days, respectively. They worked together for 2 days, after which B was replaced by C and the job was finished in the next 3 days. In how many days will C alone finish 50% of the job?
questions.questionHtml: A and B can finish a job in 10 days and 5 days, respectively. They worked together for 2 days, after which B was replaced by C and the job was finished in the next 3 days. In how many days will C alone finish 50% of the job?
questions.solution:
Efficiency of A = 10/10 = 1 unit/day, Efficiency of B = 10/5 = 2 units/day

Effective efficiency of A and B = 1 + 2 = 3 units/day

A and B work for 2 days. So, work completed = 3 × 2 units ⇒ 6 units

Remaining work = (10 – 6) units ⇒ 4 units

A and C can complete the remaining work in 3 days. So, A and C's one day work = 4/3 units

C's one-day work = (4/3) – 1 ⇒ 1/3 unit/day

C can complete 50% of work in \(\frac{10 × 50\%}{\frac{1}{3}}\) days ⇒ 5 × 3 = 15 days

questions.question: Rama alone can do a work in 5 days working 4 hours a day. Seema alone can do the same work in 3 days working 10 hours a day. How many hours do they need to work together in a day to complete the same work in 6 days?
questions.questionHtml: Rama alone can do a work in 5 days working 4 hours a day. Seema alone can do the same work in 3 days working 10 hours a day. How many hours do they need to work together in a day to complete the same work in 6 days?
questions.solution:
If they want to finish the work in 6 days, and they work together at the combined rate of 1/12 of the work per hour, then they need to work:

⇒ 6 days × x hours/day = 1 work  ⇒ x = 1 work / (6 days × 1/12 work/hour) ⇒ x = 1 / (6/12) = 2 hours/day

questions.question: Pranjal takes twice as much time as Vikram or thrice as much time as Ashwin to finish a piece of work. Working together, they can finish the work in 6 days. Vikram can do the work alone in:
questions.questionHtml: Pranjal takes twice as much time as Vikram or thrice as much time as Ashwin to finish a piece of work. Working together, they can finish the work in 6 days. Vikram can do the work alone in:
questions.solution:
let the efficiency of pranjal be x 

Then efficiency of vikram = 2x, Efficiency of Ashwin = 3x

Total efficiencies = x + 2x + 3x = 6x 

Total days taken to work together = 6 , Total unit = 6x × 6 = 36x

Now, vikram can do the work in = 36x/2x = 18

questions.question: Teena does half of a task in 6 days. Later, with Shyam’s help, she completes the remaining work in 4 days. Shyam alone can finish the entire work in:
questions.questionHtml: Teena does half of a task in 6 days. Later, with Shyam’s help, she completes the remaining work in 4 days. Shyam alone can finish the entire work in:
questions.solution:
Given:

Teena does half of a task in 6 days.

With Shyam's help, she completes the remaining work in 4 days.

Formula used:

Work done by Teena in 6 days = 1/2 of the task.

Work done by Teena in 1 day = 1/12 of the task.

Let Shyam's 1 day work be 1/x of the task.

Combined work done by Teena and Shyam in 4 days = 1/2 of the task.

Calculation:

Teena's 1 day work = 1/12

Teena and Shyam's combined 1 day work = 1/4

⇒ 4(Teena's 1 day work + Shyam's 1 day work) = 1/2

⇒ 4(1/12 + 1/x) = 1/2

⇒ 1/12 + 1/x = 1/8

⇒ 1/x = 1/8 - 1/12

⇒ 1/x = (3 - 2)/24

⇒ 1/x = 1/24

⇒ x = 24

∴ The correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: A works 5.4 times as fast as B, and A takes 22 days less than B to complete the job when each works alone. Calculate the number of days taken to complete the same job if A and B work together.
questions.questionHtml: A works 5.4 times as fast as B, and A takes 22 days less than B to complete the job when each works alone. Calculate the number of days taken to complete the same job if A and B work together.
questions.solution:
Time ratio of A : B = 1 : 5.4

Time ratio of A : B = 5 : 27

So A takes 5x days B takes 27x days 

As per the question, 27x - 5x = 22 ⇒ x = 1

So A takes 5 days and B takes 27 days 

So they together take,  ⇒ (27 × 5) / 32 = \(4\frac{7}{32}\)days

questions.question: A can do 2/5 of a work in 6 days and B can do 2/3 of the same work in 12 days. A and B worked together for 6 days. C alone completes the remaining work in 8 days. A and C, working together, will compete the same work in:
questions.questionHtml: A can do 2/5 of a work in 6 days and B can do 2/3 of the same work in 12 days. A and B worked together for 6 days. C alone completes the remaining work in 8 days. A and C, working together, will compete the same work in:
questions.solution:
A can do 2/5 of work in 6 days

A can complete the whole work in 6 × 5/2 = 15

B can do 2/3 of work in 12 days

B can complete the whole work in 12 × 3/2 = 18 days

Total work = 90

Work done by A and B in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 11 × 6 = 66

Remaining work = 90 – 66 = 24

Let efficiency of C be x.

⇒ 8 × x = 24

⇒ x = 24/8 = 3

So, efficiency of C is = 3

A and C will complete the same work in 90/(6 + 3) = 90/9 = 10 days

questions.question: A is thrice as efficient as B. A takes 24 days less than B to complete a work. If they work together, in how many days, will the work be completed?
questions.questionHtml: A is thrice as efficient as B. A takes 24 days less than B to complete a work. If they work together, in how many days, will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
Alternate MethodRatio of time taken by A and B = 1 ∶ 3

Ratio of time efficiency A and B = 3 ∶ 1

(3 - 1) units = 24

⇒ 2 units = 24

⇒ 1 units = 12

Total work = 12 × 3 × 1 = 36

Time taken by both A and B = 36/(3 + 1) = 9 days

Traditional method:

Given:

A is thrice efficient than B.

Calculation:

Ratio of time taken by A and B = 1 : 3.

Let number of days taken by A and B to complete work be a days and 3a days respectively.

⇒ 3a - a = 24

⇒ a = 12

A and B can complete work in 12 days and 36 days respectively.

Then,

⇒ 1/12 + 1/36 = 1/9

∴ In 9 days work will be completed when both work together.

questions.question: Tarun is twice as good as Tripti in doing a work. Together, they can complete the work in 16 days. In how many days can Tripti alone complete the same work?
questions.questionHtml: Tarun is twice as good as Tripti in doing a work. Together, they can complete the work in 16 days. In how many days can Tripti alone complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Tarun's 1 day's work = 2x, Tripti's 1 day's work = x

Combined 1 day's work = 3x = 1/16 ⇒ Solving: 3x = 1/16 ⇒ x = 1/48

Tripti alone: 48 days

questions.question: If 8 men or 16 women or 32 boys can do a piece of work in 8 months, then in how many months can 4 men, 4 women and 4 boys together complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: If 8 men or 16 women or 32 boys can do a piece of work in 8 months, then in how many months can 4 men, 4 women and 4 boys together complete the work?
questions.solution:
Work done by 8 men in 8 months: 1 man's work in 1 month = 1 / (8 × 8) = 1 / 64


4 men = 4 / 64 = 1 / 16

1 woman's work in 1 month = 1 / (16 × 8) = 1 / 128,4 women = 4 / 128 = 1 / 32

1 boy's work in 1 month = 1 / (32 × 8) = 1 / 256,4 boys = 4 / 256 = 1 / 64,


Total work done by 4 men, 4 women, and 4 boys in 1 month: 1 / 16 + 1 / 32 + 1 / 64 = 4 / 64 + 2 / 64 + 1 / 64 = 7/64

Time = 64 / 7 ≈ \(9 \frac{1}{7}\) months

questions.question: Pipes A and B together can fill a tank in 16 hours, whereas pipe C alone can empty the full tank in 24 hours. A and B were opened together for 10 hours and then closed. Pipe C was then opened. The tank will now be emptied by C in:
questions.questionHtml: Pipes A and B together can fill a tank in 16 hours, whereas pipe C alone can empty the full tank in 24 hours. A and B were opened together for 10 hours and then closed. Pipe C was then opened. The tank will now be emptied by C in:
questions.solution:
Given:-

(A + B) fill a tank in = 16 Hours

C can empty in = 24 Hours

Calculation:-

(A + B) fill a tank in 1 hour = 1/16

∴ (A + B) fill a tank in 10 hours = \(\large{\frac{1}{16}}\) × 10 = Available quantity in tank

C emptied the tank in 1 hour = 1/24

∴ Time taken by C in emptied the tank = (10/16)/(1/24)

Time taken by C = 240/16 = 15 hours.

Shortcut Trick

The efficiency of A and B is 3 and the efficiency of C is (-2)

Work done by pipe A and B in 10 hours = 3 × 10 = 30

Pipe C empty 30 units in 30/2 = 15 hours

∴ Required time is 15 hours.

questions.question: R, S and T can finish a work in 20, 15 and 10 days, respectively. R works on all days and S and T work on alternate days with T starting the work on the first day. In how many days is the work finished?
questions.questionHtml: R, S and T can finish a work in 20, 15 and 10 days, respectively. R works on all days and S and T work on alternate days with T starting the work on the first day. In how many days is the work finished?
questions.solution:
Let the total work be 30 units(LCM of 20, 15, and 10).

Efficiency of R, S and T = 1.5,2 and 3

On the first day, R and T work = 4.5 units

On the second day, R and S work = 3.5 units

2 day's work → 8 unit ⇒ 6  day's work → 24 unit ⇒ 7 day's work → 28.5 unit

The remaining work of 1.5 unit is done by R and S in = 1.5/3.5 ⇒ 3/7

Total time = 7 + 3/7 = 52/7

questions.question: A, B and C can complete a work in x, 30 and 45 days, respectively. B and C worked together for 6 days. The remaining work was completed by A alone in 12 days. The value of x is:
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C can complete a work in x, 30 and 45 days, respectively. B and C worked together for 6 days. The remaining work was completed by A alone in 12 days. The value of x is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Time taken to complete the work by A = x days

Time taken to complete the work by B = 30 days

Time taken to complete the work by C = 45 days

Time taken to complete the work by B and C together = 6 days

Remaining work completed by A = 12 days

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

LCM of 30 and 45 is 90

Efficiency of B = 90/30 = 3 units/day

Efficiency of C = 90/45 = 2 units/day

Total units of work by B and C together = [(3 + 2) × 6]

⇒ 30 units

Efficiency of B and C together = (90 – 30) = 60 units

Efficiency of A = (60/12) = 5 units/day

Hence, A can complete the whole work in = (90/5) days

⇒ x = 18 days

∴ The value of x is 18

questions.question: P and Q can do a job in 24 days, Q and R can do it in 30 days, while P and R can do it in 40 days. X is four times as efficient as P, Y is half as efficient as Q, and Z is 2.5 times as efficient as R. Determine the number of days required to complete the same job if X, Y and Z work together.
questions.questionHtml: P and Q can do a job in 24 days, Q and R can do it in 30 days, while P and R can do it in 40 days. X is four times as efficient as P, Y is half as efficient as Q, and Z is 2.5 times as efficient as R. Determine the number of days required to complete the same job if X, Y and Z work together.
questions.solution:
Let total work is 120 units ( LCM of 24, 30 , and 40 and)

The efficiency of  P+Q  = 120 /24 ⇒ 5 units.The efficiency of Q+R = 120 / 30 ⇒ 4 units .The efficiency of P+R = 120 / 40 ⇒ 3 units

Total efficiency of P + Q + R is (4+ 5 + 3) / 2 = 6

The efficiency of  P is 6 - 4 = 2 units.  The efficiency of  X is 2 × 4 = 8 units. 

The efficiency of  Q is 6 - 3 = 3 units.  The efficiency of  Y is 3 × .5 = 1.5 units

The efficiency of  R is 6 - 5 = 1 unit.  The efficiency of  Z is 1 × 2.5 = 2.5 units

Total efficiency of X + Y + Z is (8+ 1.5 + 2.5)  = 12 units.

The number of days required to complete the same job if X, Y and Z work together is, 120 /12 = 10days

If A and B alone can do the work in (x + 8) and (x + 18) days respectively.

x2 = 144

x = 12

So, 5/6 of the work done by A and B in = 12 × (5/6) = 10 days

questions.question: 3 men and 5 women together can complete a work in 6 days, whereas 4 men and 9 women together can do it in 4 days. How many women are required to do the same work in 7 days?
questions.questionHtml: 3 men and 5 women together can complete a work in 6 days, whereas 4 men and 9 women together can do it in 4 days. How many women are required to do the same work in 7 days?
questions.solution:
Given:-

3 men + 5 women = 6 days

4 men + 9 women = 4 days

Calculation:-

Let efficiency of 1 man and 1 woman be x and y respectively

As we know,

Total work = Total work

According to the question

(3x + 5y)6 = (4x + 9y)4

18x + 30y = 16x + 36y

18x – 16x = 36 – 30y

2x = 6y

x/y = 6/2 = 3/1

x : y = 3 : 1

Total work = (3 × 3 + 5 × 1) 6 = 84

Let n women complete the whole work in 7 days, then

n × 1 × 7 = 84

n = 84/7 = 12

∴ Required number of women is 12.

questions.question: A can complete a certain piece of work in 40 days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 28% more efficient than B. They work together for 5 days. The remaining work will be complete by B alone, in:
questions.questionHtml: A can complete a certain piece of work in 40 days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 28% more efficient than B. They work together for 5 days. The remaining work will be complete by B alone, in:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Efficiency ratio A : B : C = 100 : 125 : (125 × 1.28) = 100 : 125 : 160 = 20 : 25 : 32.

Total Work = Efficiency of A × Days = 20 × 40 = 800 units.

5 days work of (A+B+C) = 5 × (20 + 25 + 32) = 5 × 77 = 385 units.

Remaining work = 800 − 385 = 415 units.

Time taken by B alone = 415 ÷ 25 = 16.6 days = 16(3/5) days.

∴ The correct answer is 16(3/5) days.

Alternate Method

Given: A completes work in 40 days. Efficiency of B is 25% more than A. Efficiency of C is 28% more than B.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 40 800 20
B 32 25
C 25 32

⇒ Efficiency of A = 20 (assumed to make B = 25 and C = 32)

⇒ Total Work = 40 × 20 = 800 units

⇒ Combined Efficiency (A+B+C) = 20 + 25 + 32 = 77 units/day

⇒ Work done in 5 days = 77 × 5 = 385 units

⇒ Remaining Work = 800 − 385 = 415 units

⇒ Time taken by B = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of B

⇒ Time = 415 ÷ 25 = 83 ÷ 5 = 16(3/5) days

∴ The correct answer is 16(3/5) days.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. If A is x% more efficient than B, Efficiency Ratio A:B = (100+x):100.

Total Work Formula

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. This remains constant for a specific piece of work regardless of the number of people working.

Work Done by Group

When people work together, their efficiencies are additive. Combined Efficiency = E1 + E2 + ... + En.

questions.question: To do a certain work, A is 40% more efficient than B. Working together, they can do the same work in 15 days. A started the work and left after 15 days. B and C together completed the remaining work in next 10 days. C alone can do one-third of the original work in:

Time = Work/Efficiency

A complete in 15 days = 15 × 7 = 105 work

C will take time to complete one-third of the original work = (180/3)/2.5 = 24 days

∴ C alone can do one-third of the original work in 24 days

questions.question: A can complete a work in 60 days. B is 25% more efficient than A. They work together for 15 days. C alone completes the remaining work in 14 days. B and C together will complete \(\frac{5}{8}\) th part of the original work in:

questions.solution:
Given:

Time taken to complete a work by A = 60 days

B is 25% more efficient than A 

(A + B) worked together = 15 days

Time taken to complete the remaining work by C = 14 days

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

Let the efficiency of A be x

B is 25% more efficient than A

⇒ (25/100)x = 1x/4

Efficient of A = 4

Efficient of B = (4 + 1) = 5

Total work = (4 × 60) = 240 units

A and B worked together for 15 days = [(5 + 4) × 15]

⇒ (9 × 15) = 135 units

Remaining work = (240 – 135) = 105 units

Time taken to complete the remaining work by C = (105/14) 

⇒ 15/2 = 7.5

Time taken by B and C to complete the 5/8th part of original work = [240/(5 + 7.5) × 5/8]

⇒ (240/12.5 × 5/8)

⇒ (6 × 2)

⇒ 12 days

∴ The required time is 12 days

Shortcut Trick

So, total efficiency of A and B = 9

In 15 days work of A + B = 9 × 15 = 135 units

Remaining (240 - 135) = 105 units will complete by C in 14 days

So, C in one day = 7.5 units

Time taken by B and C to complete the 5/8th part of original work = [240/(5 + 7.5) × 5/8] = 12 days

questions.solution:
(12M + 12W) × 9 = (6M + 15W) × 12

⇒ 108M + 108W = 72M + 180W ⇒ 36M = 72W ⇒ M : W = 2 : 1

Total work = (6M + 15W) × 12 ⇒ (6 × 2 + 15 × 1) × 12 ⇒ 324

 9 women to complete the half of the work = 324/2 × 1/9 ⇒ 18 days

questions.question: A can finish a work in 15 days, B can finish the same work in 25 days. They work together for 5 days. The rest of the work is finished by A and C in 4 days. Then C alone can finish the work in:
questions.questionHtml: A can finish a work in 15 days, B can finish the same work in 25 days. They work together for 5 days. The rest of the work is finished by A and C in 4 days. Then C alone can finish the work in:
questions.solution:
Let total work be 75 units ( LCM of 15 and 25 is 75)

The efficiency of A ⇒ 75 /15 = 5 units

The efficiency of B   ⇒ 75 / 25 = 3 units

The efficiency of A+B, ⇒ (5 + 3) units = 8 units

In 5 days total work done is 8 × 5 = 40 units. Remaining work 75 - 40 = 35 units

In the last 4 days, A does 4 × 5 = 20 units

Remaining work 35 - 20 = 15 units done by C in 4 days

So C does 75 units in (75 / 15) × 4 = 20 days.
